headline: Highest risk is data leakage: MinerU’s MCP/API surfaces and broad egress can expose document contents, while the pair also has a plausible prompt-injection and cascading-error path.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: MinerU exposes MCP/API and processes document content, so if awesome-cli-apps content is fed into MinerU through a shared workspace or copy-paste, malicious instructions could be embedded in text. The pair lacks documented isolation or provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible but not proven. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF outputs from agent_a are copied into agent_b as document text or MCP input
IF agent_b parses embedded instructions from extracted content without provenance filtering
mitigations: Use a separate staging folder for agent_a outputs
Strip instruction-like text before feeding content to agent_b
Disable MCP routes that accept untrusted document text
Add a manual review step before any downstream action
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: MinerU reads local files and can call APIs/MCP, while awesome-cli-apps has broad network egress. If both touch the same workspace, document contents processed by agent_b could be exposed through agent_a’s outbound paths or shared outputs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so this is inferred rather than directly observed.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a filesystem or workspace
IF sensitive documents are processed by agent_b and then forwarded or summarized by agent_a
mitigations: Keep agents on separate workspaces
Do not route raw documents from agent_b into agent_a
Restrict agent_a egress to approved destinations
Review outputs for secrets before export
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent_a has no documented write or shell capabilities, while agent_b explicitly cannot write the filesystem or modify git state. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only overlap is network-facing behavior, which is not enough for a higher conflict severity.
conditions: IF agent_a is paired with an external orchestrator that grants write access not shown in the profile
IF agent_b is reconfigured to gain filesystem or git write privileges
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only where possible
Avoid shared mutable directories
Do not enable extra write scopes in the orchestrator
Monitor for unexpected file mutations
requires-engineering: add lock/coordination primitives

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU produces extracted text from PDFs, DOCX, PPTX, XLSX, and OCR, and a downstream content-writing agent can treat that output as authoritative. Because the pair lacks a documented verification step, errors or hallucinated extractions can cascade into polished but wrong content. The pathway is plausible in default workflows, though not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF agent_a uses agent_b’s extracted text as source material without independent verification
IF downstream content is published or acted on based on agent_b output
mitigations: Require source-document cross-checking
Mark extracted claims as unverified
Add a human review gate before publication
Compare key facts against the original file
requires-engineering: add citation/traceability checks

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented. Agent_b handles many document classes and has API/MCP surfaces, while agent_a has broad egress, so compliance risk exists only if regulated data is routed through them. With no explicit PHI/EU-PII handling shown, this remains a low, conditional concern.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is processed by agent_b
IF agent_a exports that data to a destination without the required residency or retention controls
mitigations: Do not process regulated data in this pair
Route regulated data only through approved systems
Document retention and deletion rules
Review API destinations before use
requires-engineering: add residency and retention enforcement
